title: Monthly Alignment Meeting
narration: Item one on the agenda is the agenda. The projector shows a slide titled Where We Are. Nobody can say.

signs.label: Who interrupts whom
signs.text: {holder} talks over {ignored} twice before the first slide. {ignored} apologises both times.

signs.label: Who everyone looks at
signs.text: When a question is asked, {bystander} and {ignored} both glance at {holder} before answering.

signs.label: Who gets ignored
signs.text: {ignored} makes a suggestion. Four minutes later {bystander} makes the same one, to general approval.

results.body: Hugh does not look at you. The next agenda has your name on it, spelled correctly, and people start holding doors.
Hugh thanks you, using the name of someone who left in March. Several people make a note of that, and of you.

options.label: Agree warmly with Dennis, your boss

results.body: Dennis nods at you, as one might nod at a useful chair. Afterwards Dennis uses your first name, and it is nearly correct.
Dennis is delighted and says so. Nobody else looks up. Your agreement with your official boss has been noted by your official boss.
Priya writes your name down. It is the first time anyone here has. Two people notice, and one of them passes you a biscuit.
Priya thanks you for your input, in the voice kept for people who have not given any. The meeting carries on, as though a window had briefly rattled.
Marjorie looks at you over the top of the reading glasses for some time. The next morning your broken chair has been replaced. No ticket was raised.
Marjorie smiles and asks whether you would mind taking the minutes. You are now the person who takes the minutes.
Callum makes a small note and does not look up. By Thursday a project you had never heard of has your name on the good half of it.
Callum looks surprised, then grateful, then worried for you. The agenda moves on without either of you.

options.label: Suggest that what this calls for is strategic patience

results.body: Dennis looks pleased, then alarmed, then pleased to have thought of it first. By lunchtime the phrase is in the minutes, credited to the team.
There is a silence, of the respectful kind. You are asked to say more. You say the same thing again, more slowly. You have been asked to lead a working group on it.

options.label: Say nothing and write something down

results.body: You write key takeaways on your pad and underline it. Nobody asks you anything. You are recorded as present, which is the highest rating available at your grade.
